source: In-game measurements reported by Flavien; manual timing and step counts. No recordings are redistributed.

experiments.observation: 200 steps at a constant 90 km/h covered 1 km.
experiments.limits: A second, shorter 137 m measurement was consistent within one step.

experiments.observation: Four simulation seconds per day; 365 days per game year.
experiments.limits: Maintenance-per-journey values assume this calendar speed and continuous service.

experiments.observation: 90 km/h to rest: 50 steps (10 s). Metroliner, observed 158 km/h to rest: 87 steps (17.4 s).
experiments.limits: The observed starting speed is rounded. Broader tests could reveal vehicle differences.

experiments.observation: Metroliner: 38 passengers, 2 cars × 1.5; loading measured at 12.45 s, compared with 12.67 s predicted. Roter Pfeil: 19 additional passengers in 19 steps (3.8 s), one car × 5.
experiments.adopted: 1 passenger/s per multiplier per car, applied to both loading and unloading.
experiments.limits: Equal contributions from all cars remain an assumption. Step-by-step runs sometimes delayed the last passengers.

experiments.observation: Approximately 2–2.5 s before departure; repeated step measurements also showed delays before unloading and loading.
experiments.adopted: 6 s per terminal: 2 before unloading, 2 before loading, 2 before departure.
experiments.limits: Approximate calibration, not a universal verified constant.

experiments.observation: Identical trains with 60 and 2 passengers appeared to accelerate at the same rate in a visual drag race.
experiments.adopted: Use empty train mass regardless of occupancy.
experiments.limits: No precise timing was recorded; this does not exclude an effect below visual resolution.

experiments.observation: On the same station pair: 60 passengers earned $1,179,000; Metroliner, 38 passengers, $747,118; Roter Pfeil, 20 passengers, $396,260.
experiments.adopted: Assume the same fare per passenger when comparing equal throughput on the same route.
experiments.limits: Approximately $19,650–$19,813 per passenger in these runs. One route cannot establish the complete pricing formula; station-to-station distance was only approximate.

experiments.observation: Flavien recovered loadSpeedFactor values: freight 0.0625, passengers 1. MAN 19.304, multiplier 3, no bonuses, simulation x1: loading from 1 to 16 took about 85 s (freight availability unchecked); unloading 16 to 0 took about 80 s. Truck pauses between operations reported as 2 s.
experiments.adopted: Fixed category factors 0.0625 freight / 1 passengers, multiplied once by vehicle loading speed and freight facility bonuses. 2 s before each active transfer operation and departure: 6 s per terminal with unloading plus loading; 4 s with only one operation (8 s per empty-return round trip).
experiments.limits: Factor source reported from a prior investigation, not independently extracted. Manual timings approximate. The user confirmed the 6 s / 4 s distinction; extension of truck delays to buses/trams remains an assumption.
